partner_result.actual_use: Retained the partner whole-product logarithmic envelope and square level-set layer cake, inserted subprobability mass caps, introduced two tunable product thresholds, and optimized the resulting inequality.

new_results.statement: For cap-one subprobability densities u,v of masses m,n, p_{UV}(z)<=m/R+n/S+2log_+(RS/|z|) for every R,S>0.

For cap-one subprobability u,v,w of masses m,n,r, Q=2aUV+lambda Y^2+arbitrary affine, theta=2sqrt(|a|mn/|lambda|)/r gives ||p_Q^(sub)||_inf <= (2r/|a|)Phi(theta), Phi=2sqrt(theta) for theta<=1 and 2+log theta for theta>=1.

For probability marginals and |a|,|lambda|>=1, ||p_{2aUV+lambda Y^2+affine}||_inf <= 4+2log2 = 5.386294361119891..., and the same constant survives arbitrary outside original-coordinate conditioning/couplings.

At a=lambda=1, splitting only the active square law into masses r_j and summing positive certificates costs at most 4+2log2+2H(r), hence equal N refinement introduces 2logN while whole-law localization has no such tax.

unresolved_implication: From bare s_3(A)>=1, before active fragmentation force either a whole original-coordinate hyperbolic pair plus a genuinely disjoint square with quantitative scales, or an existing aggregate ridge/volume/hub/pair/receiver exit. Same-bank overlap remains open.
next_step: Try to replace the disjoint-square requirement by a same-bank curved receiver estimate that retains the whole product until the final layer-cake step; do not split active high peaks.
